title: Data Quality and AI Outputs
summary: Students trace the causal chain from a specific data-quality problem to the specific output mistake it causes, and separate the quality of a dataset from its size.
objectives: Explain, with an example, how higher- or lower-quality data changes an AI output.
Predict the effect on the output when the data quality is degraded or improved.
Distinguish the quality of a dataset from the quantity of data in it.

sections.heading: Data Quality and AI Outputs
body: Imagine teaching a younger cousin to recognise dates using a photo album. If half the photos are blurry and one photo is actually a stone, incorrectly labelled as a date, what will your cousin get wrong? An AI learns the same way you would teach - from the examples it is shown. Today you become a data detective who can predict an AI's mistakes just by studying its data.

sections.heading: I can…
items: I can explain, using a clear example, how the quality of data changes what an AI produces.
I can predict whether an output will get better or worse when the data is made cleaner or noisier, and say why.
I can tell the difference between the amount of data and the quality of data.

terms.definition: How accurate, complete, consistent, and representative a dataset is.
The name attached to an example that tells the model what it is.
Irrelevant or inconsistent detail in data that confuses the pattern.
The data covers the real range of cases the model will meet.
A step-by-step link from a cause to its effect.

sections.heading: The model learns from its examples
body: An AI model is not filled with rules that a person typed. Instead it studies a dataset and adjusts itself to match the patterns it finds.
This means the dataset is really the model's teacher. If the teacher shows wrong examples, the model learns the wrong lesson - and it does so confidently.

sections.label: How a data problem becomes an output mistake
sections.heading: One flaw, traced all the way to the answer
sections.altText: A chain of three boxes: a data problem leads to a wrong learned pattern, which leads to a wrong output.
sections.caption: This is the chain you trace on your worksheet. Start at the data, not the answer.

nodes.label: The output is wrong
nodes.detail: it calls a pebble a date

sections.heading: Quality is not the same as quantity
body: It is tempting to think more data always helps. But a huge dataset full of mistakes just teaches the wrong pattern more strongly.

A small, clean, well-chosen dataset can beat a giant messy one. Before trusting any output, a careful builder checks the quality of the data behind it - and never puts personal or identifying information into a tool.

sections.label: Your dataset card
sections.heading: What a dataset card shows you
sections.intro: Your teacher gives you a card describing one dataset. Read it in this order — the flaw is never announced, you have to find it.

entries.asks: How many items are there, and what is each one a picture of?
entries.test: A small set is not automatically a bad one.

entries.asks: What is each example called? Is every label correct?
entries.test: One wrong label teaches one wrong lesson.

entries.asks: Does the set cover the real range of cases, or only some of them?
entries.test: A gap is as damaging as an error.

entries.asks: Is anything blurry, inconsistent or irrelevant?
entries.test: Noise makes the pattern harder to find.

sections.label: Let's try it - hands-on
sections.heading: Let's try it - hands-on
body: You will study a dataset card, predict the exact mistake the AI will make, then watch the real outputs to check your detective work.
items: Read your dataset card and note how each item is labelled.
Decide the quality problem: error, gap, or noise.
Predict one exact output mistake and write it down before the reveal.
Compare your prediction with the revealed clean and degraded outputs.
Write one sentence linking the data cause to the output effect.

sections.heading: Think about it
items: When could a bigger dataset actually make an AI worse?
How can an output be wrong and still sound completely sure of itself?

sections.heading: My reflection
items: Write one thing you can now predict about an AI just by looking at its data.
Name one place in daily life where poor-quality data could lead to an unfair result.

worksheet.title: Week 1 - Core - Worksheet | Data Quality and AI Outputs

questions.prompt: A team trains an AI to spot dates in photos. Every photo and label is correct except one: a photo of a small grey stone has been labelled "date". Which mistake should you predict in the AI's output?

options.text: It will sometimes look at a small grey stone and call it a date.
It will refuse to answer whenever it is shown a stone.
It will start calling real dates stones.
It will be unaffected, because one wrong photo is too small a part of the dataset to matter.

feedback.correct: Right - the model copies the pattern in its examples, so one stone labelled "date" teaches it that a small grey lump can be a date, and it says so confidently.
feedback.incorrect: Follow the chain from the data: the stone was labelled "date", so the model learns that shape counts as a date and applies that lesson to new stones.

questions.prompt: A team has 40 date photos that are clear and correctly labelled. They add 4,000 more photos, but many labels in that new batch are wrong. Select every statement that is a good prediction of what happens.

options.text: The dataset is now much bigger, but lower in quality.
The wrong pattern will be taught more strongly than before, because thousands of examples now repeat it.
Knowing only that the dataset grew does not tell you the outputs will be better.
The outputs will improve, because the AI now has far more examples to learn from.
The new photos cannot do any harm, because the 40 correct photos are still in the set.

feedback.correct: Yes - quantity and quality are different things, and a huge dataset full of mistakes just teaches the wrong pattern more strongly.
feedback.incorrect: More data only helps if the data is good: adding thousands of wrong labels repeats the wrong lesson, and the correct 40 cannot cancel that out.

questions.prompt: Four teams trained the same AI on different versions of a date-photo dataset. Match each dataset to the output you should expect from it.

left.text: A few stones are labelled "date"; everything else is correct.
Every photo is correct, but the set contains only dark brown dates - no yellow ones.
Half the photos are blurry and the labels are written as "date", "dat" and "DATE".
Only 12 photos, but all clear, all correctly labelled, and covering every kind of date.

right.text: It confidently calls small stones dates.
It handles brown dates well but gets yellow dates wrong, because it never saw one.
It is unsure and inconsistent on every kind of photo, because the pattern is hard to pick out.
It gives mostly correct answers, even though it learned from a small set.

feedback.correct: Well matched - an error teaches a false pattern, a gap leaves a whole case unseen, noise blurs the pattern everywhere, and a small clean set can still do well.
feedback.incorrect: Ask what each flaw teaches the model: a wrong label teaches a wrong thing, a missing kind of date cannot be learned at all, and noise makes every case harder.

questions.prompt: Put these four steps in order to trace how one problem in the data becomes one wrong answer.

items.text: A photo of a stone is put into the dataset with the label "date".
The model studies the dataset and adjusts itself to match the patterns it finds.
The model now treats small round grey objects as dates.
Shown a new photo of a pebble, the model answers "date".

feedback.correct: That is the causal chain: a problem in the data, then a pattern learned from it, then the wrong output it produces.
feedback.incorrect: Start at the data, not the answer - the flawed example comes first, the model learns from it, and only then does the wrong output appear.

questions.prompt: A team re-photographs every blurry item so it is sharp, and rewrites the labels that had been spelled three different ways. The dataset still holds exactly the same photos of exactly the same dates - none are added and none are taken away. Based on the lesson, the AI’s outputs should get better.

feedback.correct: Yes - taking out noise makes the pattern easier to learn, and that is a quality improvement even though the dataset is exactly the same size.
feedback.incorrect: The amount of data did not change, but the noise did: less blur and consistent labels make the pattern clearer, so the outputs should improve.
